summary: Jim G. Shaffer is an archaeologist and Indologist. He earned a B.A. from Arizona State University (~1961–1965) and a Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1972), later becoming professor of anthropology at Case Western Reserve University around 1972.

Jim Rheingans specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from the University of Hamburg and PhDs from the University of the West of England and Bath Spa University, supervised by David P. Jackson, Mahinda Deegalle, and Fiona Montgomery.

Jin Kyoung Choi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. A doctoral student and later postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (attested 2026), Choi also served as Lehrbeauftragte at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Jin Y. Park works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Park held an appointment as Assistant Professor of Philosophy and Religion at American University (attested 2007–2012) and served as a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong.
Jin-il Chung is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. Chung has worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities as a Mitarbeiter (attested 2008) and Redaktor (attested 2026).

Jinah Kim works in South Asian art history, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at UC Berkeley under Joanna Gottfried Williams. She has held posts at Harvard University, Vanderbilt University, and the Institute for Advanced Study (2009–2010).
Jinavijaya Muni (1888–1976) was an Indologist and historian. He founded the Rajasthan Puratana Granthamala (attested 1959) and served as Principal of Gujarat Vidyapith.

Jinbo Shi specializes in history, archaeology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Minzu University of China and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences under Jingru Wang. His appointments include positions at CASS, Minzu University, Ningxia University, and North Minzu University.
Jinchuan Wan works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Wan held professor positions at both National Central University and Fo Guang University (both attested 2010).
Jing Yin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 1995). Yin held a post as Director at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2006–2010).

Jing-shen Tao is a historian and Sinologist. He studied at National Taiwan University and Indiana University Bloomington (Ph.D. ~1965–1969). He served as Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–2000) and at Academia Sinica (~1990).
Jingru Wang (1903–1990) was a linguist and historian. He studied at Tsinghua University (~1925–1929) and held a post at Minzu University of China (~1952–1986).
Jingyi Yang works in Indology, Tibetology, and computational studies. Yang studied at the University of Hamburg and held a post there as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin (attested 2026).

Jinhua Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Chen completed graduate studies at McMaster University and postdoctoral research under Noritoshi Aramaki at Kyoto University, later serving as professor of East Asian Buddhism at the University of British Columbia (attested 2008–2018).

Jinhua Jia is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned a PhD at the University of Colorado Boulder under Paul W. Kroll. Jia held positions at Harvard, HKPU, CU Boulder, IAS, and the National Humanities Center (2014–2015).
Jinling He is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Hiroki Okumura.
Jinping Liao is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.

Jinshi Fan is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University (~1958–1963) under Su Bai. She served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy (1984–2014) and has held a post at Lanzhou University.

Jinzhang Peng (1937–2017) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He served at Wuhan University (~1963–1986) and held positions as dean of the archaeological institute and researcher/professor at the Dunhuang Academy (~1986–2017).
Jiro Abe (1883–1959) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1907). He held academic posts at Japan Women's University (~1913–1923) and Tohoku University (~1923–1944).
